audit.why: EVEN / 5.5/10 fits 47.8% over 159 games: Neeko dominates levels 1-5 against the weakest early laner in the lane, and loses the long game to a drain tank.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart handed Neeko 6 of 7 stages including 2+ items, while the win rate is 47.8% and the page's own late text says Vladimir's sustain overtakes.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts AP into HP and back, and Hemoplague amps damage and heals per champion hit on a flat 120s. Two-item Vladimir is the favourite; the row argued with the prose under it.
audit.corrected: 2+ items moved to Vladimir on both layers with matching whys; levels 4-5 and first item settled on Neeko on both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states Sanguine Pool's cooldown, nor that Tides of Blood is blocked by units, nor that Transfusion costs no mana.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 down to 16s at rank 5 for 2 seconds untargetable — that is the single window Pop Blossom must respect. Transfusion is free and reaches 4.6s at rank 5, so chip poke is healed back. Tides of Blood (13s->5s) is paid in health and enemy units block it.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns and the minion-block written into breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad and the don'ts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds was mentioned only in the itemization line and nowhere in the mid-game plan.
audit.why: Both Transfusion and Hemoplague heal him; anti-heal timing decides every extended fight.
audit.corrected: breakdown.mid and report[5] now name Grievous Wounds against a 120s Hemoplague.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the cooldowns/tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Copy-paste bleed — title and body describe different things.
audit.corrected: Each rewritten to its own title using Vladimir's numbers.

edits.before: Late Neeko is an ambush: disguise into their formation, R the clump, and root whatever scatters.

edits.before: You stay favoured late by flanking and bursting him before his drain-tank scaling peaks.
edits.after: By two items his drain-tank scaling beats you unless you land the pick before the fight.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Check it before every step-up. - W Shapesplitter clone is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and still 16s at rank 5: 2 seconds untargetable, so hold R until it is spent. - Transfusion drops from 9s to 4.6s — he heals off the wave forever. - Tides of Blood is 13s to 5s and minions block it.

edits.before: E his step-up, Q the rooted target for all three blooms, auto the passive, walk — the full package is half a bar at level 3.
edits.after: E his step-up, Q the rooted target so the seed blooms again, then auto for the passive — his answer costs health he needs.

edits.before: Q-poking with E banked 'for safety' until the lane forgets your kill threat exists — the root IS the threat; the bloom is just the receipt.
edits.after: Chip poke that Transfusion just heals back — his Q costs no mana and hits 4.6s at rank 5, so trade in packages that root first or don't trade.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling your commit, healing the lane back with Transfusion, and scaling into a drain tank.

edits.before: Poke blooms and tell lies — your trades are even and your information war isn't. Every clone he answers wrong is tempo.
edits.after: Vladimir's early is the weakest in the lane — Transfusion is 9s at rank 1 and Tides of Blood costs him health he cannot spare.

edits.before: Post-6, hunt clumps: disguise into the wave, R the river contest, root the scatter. One good crouch is a won objective.
edits.after: Post-6 he answers with Hemoplague every 120s — fight while it is down, and start Grievous Wounds before the drain items land.

edits.before: Carry through deception — every fight you start disguised begins 5v4 in spirit; your job is the patience the crouch demands.
edits.after: Carry by removing him from the fight — E root plus Pop Blossom on a Vladimir who has already spent his 28s pool ends him.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Q him as he steps into Transfusion range — 600 on his Q against 800 on yours, so the seed blooms on him for free.

edits.before: E his step-up, Q the rooted target for all three blooms, auto the passive, walk — the full package is half a bar at level 3.
edits.after: Send the clone one way and walk the other — Vladimir has 2 seconds of pool and no other escape, so a wrong read leaves him stuck.

edits.before: Root the step-up, triple-bloom the root
edits.after: Root the step-up, then bloom the root

edits.before: Vladimir spends Sanguine Pool early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: E him as he walks up for Transfusion, then Q the root — pool cannot undo damage already dealt.

edits.before: That’s Vladimir’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: E is your only lockdown here — spend it on the commit, not on poke spacing.

edits.before: The clone is your scout, your fake, and your escape — spending it on idle tricks near assassin timers is how Neekos get audited.
edits.after: The clone is a 16s cooldown at rank 1 — waste it on a trick he has already seen and you have nothing left to bait the pool with.

edits.before: Trade during his key-spell window
edits.after: Dump your combo into Sanguine Pool

edits.before: Q-poking with E banked 'for safety' until the lane forgets your kill threat exists — the root IS the threat; the bloom is just the receipt.
edits.after: Pool is 2 seconds of untargetable and it eats a whole Pop Blossom — bait it with the clone or a feint, then commit while it sits on a 28s cooldown.

edits.before: Track Vladimir’s Sanguine Pool: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Vladimir’s Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5, 2 seconds untargetable. Spend R only after it, and bring Grievous Wounds.

notes: Vladimir's Sanguine Pool grants untargetability, not CC immunity, but nothing in Riot's text says whether pooling out of an existing Tangle-Barbs root ends the root — I did not claim either way (listed in unverified). packet.suspectNames flagged wants.foe[1] 'Use Sanguine Pool' as a wrong name; it is correct and was left alone. The chart contradicted the win rate (Neeko 6/7 stages at 47.8%): moved 2+ items to Vladimir on both layers and settled the two rows where full and content disagreed. Ratings left untouched throughout — the existing rating scale is not self-consistent (Neeko-winning rows and Vladimir-winning rows both sit at 6/10), so I could not tell which direction a change should move.
